chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mahfuz al-Iskaaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you want to bury the deceased, let the wisest one who enters his grave be at his head, and let him uncover his right cheek until it is exposed to the ground, and bring his mouth close to his ear and say: 'Listen, understand!' three times: 'Allah is your Lord, and Muhammad is your Prophet, and Islam is your Religion, and so-and-so is your Imam. Listen and understand'; and repeat it to him three times, this is the Talqeen (indoctrination).

key_terms.التَّلْقِين: Talqeen: The act of reciting creedal statements to the deceased in the grave to remind them of their faith.
key_terms.فُلَانٌ إِمَامُكَ: So-and-so is your Imam (referring to the specific Imam of the time).

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure and recitation for burying the deceased in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the specific etiquette for the grave burial, emphasizing the placement of the deceased on their right side facing the Qibla and the recitation of the 'Talqeen' (creedal instruction) to affirm faith in the Hereafter. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the Imamate as a core component of belief, explicitly naming the Imam alongside Allah, the Prophet, and Islam in the declaration of faith. This practice underscores the continuity of spiritual guidance from the Prophet to the Imams, ensuring the deceased enters the grave with a clear understanding of their religious authority.
